title: Move scheduled exports into worker processes
summary: Four focused changes: enqueue work, configure the producer, run bounded worker threads, and deploy the consumer independently.

context.problem: Export work runs inside the API request process. That request stays open until the export finishes; stopping the API process interrupts the in-flight job.
context.baseline: Illustrative baseline: every five minutes, cron calls the API. The API awaits buildExport(), stores the result, then replies done. There is no queued handoff or independent consumer.
context.scope: One hypothetical solution. The paths, before/after excerpts, and infrastructure below are illustrative, not inspected project files.
constraints: Accept a job only after durable queue publication; acknowledge it after storing its result.
Bound concurrency and preserve the job ID across delivery attempts.
assumptions: The broker supports durable delivery and the existing results table has a unique job ID.
The illustrative consume wrapper acknowledges only after its callback succeeds.
RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, and TeamCity are illustrative product choices here, not findings about this project.

visual.caption: The diagram shows the normal completion path: cron calls the API, the export runs in that same process, then its result is stored. The failure scenario above stops the API before completion: the in-flight export is interrupted and this attempt stores no completed result. This does not delete previous results, rule out a later retry, or prove CPU saturation.

nodes.label: API request
nodes.issue: The response cannot finish until buildExport() completes. Long exports tie request duration to job duration; there is no asynchronous job handoff.

edges.label: Invoke the API; wait for its response
Run export inside this API process
edges.issue: The export shares the API process lifetime. If that process stops before completion, the in-flight execution is interrupted; no separate consumer can continue it.

edges.label: Store the result; only then return done

scenario.condition: The API process stops while an export is still running.
scenario.cause: The request and export share the same process lifetime. There is no durable handoff to an independent consumer.
scenario.consequence: The unfinished export is interrupted: this attempt stores no completed result, and its request cannot return success. A later retry is not ruled out.

changes.title: Publish a job instead of building inline
changes.description: The producer returns a queued job handle. Export execution moves to a consumer.
changes.why: Keep long-running work outside the API request lifecycle.

code.summary: Replace one inline call with durable publication; completion becomes asynchronous.

visual.caption: Only acceptance happens in the API. The message carries the stable job ID; the queue separates producer and consumer lifecycles.

changes.title: Put routing and concurrency in configuration
changes.description: Cron keeps its schedule while queue selection and worker count become explicit settings.
changes.why: Let operations adjust execution settings without editing the producer logic.

code.summary: Preserve the existing cadence; add the queue name and a bounded worker count.

visual.caption: Config controls the schedule and routing. Cron still invokes the producer; the selected queue receives the job.

changes.title: Consume work in a bounded thread pool
changes.description: A separate consumer process starts two worker threads and persists results by job ID.
changes.why: Isolate execution from the API and cap simultaneous export work.

code.summary: Start the pool once; run each delivered job in a worker thread and upsert its result before acknowledging.

visual.caption: The boundary shows ownership: one consumer process and two threads share a worker host. Results are persisted outside that host before the process acknowledges delivery.

groups.label: export-worker-01
groups.detail: One worker host, isolated from the API server.

edges.label: Upsert by job ID, then acknowledge

changes.title: Deploy the consumer independently
changes.description: The CI/CD agent ships the API and export worker as separate services using the same queue binding.
changes.why: Restart or scale consumers without tying their lifecycle to HTTP serving.

code.summary: Add one independently managed worker service to the deployment.

visual.caption: The CI/CD agent deploys a worker host with a running consumer. Config supplies its queue binding; the existing API deployment remains in place.

manualChanges.action: Provision a durable exports.ready queue and producer/consumer access.
manualChanges.verification: A published test job survives a consumer restart.

manualChanges.action: Configure the worker's queue binding and confirm callers accept a queued job handle.
manualChanges.prerequisite: Queue access and the job-ID uniqueness constraint are confirmed.
manualChanges.verification: The consumer starts, completes a job, and persists its result before acknowledging.

impact.description: The API returns a queued job handle; completion becomes eventual. Callers must use the job ID to inspect the result.
The cadence stays the same. Queue routing and concurrency become operational settings.
At most two jobs execute per worker host. Re-delivered jobs update the same result key; execution still consumes resources.
The worker can restart independently of the API. Delivery depends on a healthy consumer and a correctly configured broker binding.

risks.title: A job can be delivered more than once
risks.condition: A consumer stops after saving a result but before acknowledging delivery.
risks.consequence: The job can run again, consuming extra resources or repeating other side effects.
risks.mitigation: Keep the stable job ID, upsert its result, and make any additional effects idempotent.

risks.title: Jobs accumulate without a healthy consumer
risks.condition: The worker is stopped or its queue binding is wrong.
risks.consequence: The API can accept jobs while completion is delayed.
risks.mitigation: Verify consumption after deployment and monitor queue age and worker health.
